prompt: Why does the lesson read the JSON into a `SessionDto` instead of straight into `StudySession`?
hint: Which of the two changes when the server changes?

choices.text: So a server change stops at the DTO
choices.why: Right: the screens read the model, and only the DTO and `toDomain()` know the wire.

choices.text: Because a data class cannot carry `@Serializable`
choices.why: `SessionDto` is itself a data class with `@Serializable`.

choices.text: Because Retrofit refuses to return a domain model
choices.why: Retrofit returns whatever the converter can read; the split is a design choice, not a rule of the library.

choices.text: To make the JSON smaller on the wire
choices.why: The DTO is a Kotlin class; it changes nothing about the bytes the server sends.

prompt: Match each mismatch between the JSON and the model to the tool the lesson uses for it.
hint: Sections 03, 04 and 05.

pairs.left: a key the app has never seen

prompt: The serialization plugin is removed from the build file. What happens to `Json.decodeFromString<SessionDto>(text)`?
hint: The annotation alone writes nothing.

choices.text: The build fails because `@Serializable` is unknown without the plugin
choices.why: The annotation comes from the library, which is still a dependency, so it compiles.

choices.text: It compiles, then fails at run time: no serializer found
choices.why: Right: no serializer was generated, and the call looks for one at run time.

choices.text: It falls back to reflection, more slowly
choices.why: kotlinx.serialization has no reflection fallback; that is Moshi's other mode.

choices.text: It returns an empty `SessionDto`
choices.why: There is no empty value to return; `id` and `minutes` have no defaults.

prompt: The round trip decoded `"done": false` and wrote the object back. Why is `done` missing from the output?
hint: Compare the value with the one in the class.

choices.text: `false` is never written by JSON libraries
choices.why: `false` is a valid JSON value and is written when asked to be.

choices.text: A `Boolean` property is skipped unless annotated
choices.why: The type does not matter; the default does.

choices.text: It equals the default, and defaults are omitted
choices.why: Right: `done` defaults to `false`, so the encoder omitted it.

choices.text: The test printed the DTO before the field was read
choices.why: The first line shows `done=false`, read correctly.

prompt: The plugin generates a nested class called `SessionDto$$___` that reads and writes each field.
hint: `find` listed three class files.

prompt: With the default `Json`, the server adds a key `room` to a session. What does the app get?
hint: The first strict line.

choices.text: The session, with `room` dropped
choices.why: That is what `ignoreUnknownKeys = true` gives, not the default.

choices.text: A `JsonDecodingException` naming the unknown key
choices.why: Right: the default refuses the whole session at `Encountered an unknown key 'room'`.

choices.text: A `MissingFieldException`
choices.why: Nothing is missing; something extra arrived.

choices.text: The session, with `room` kept in a map of extras
choices.why: A DTO has no place for keys it does not declare.

prompt: A server starts sending `"done": null` and `"minutes": null`. With `coerceInputValues = true`, what does the app get?
hint: Coercion needs a default to coerce to.

choices.text: A session with `done = false` and `minutes = 0`
choices.why: `minutes` has no default, and the library does not invent zero.

choices.text: A session with both fields `null`
choices.why: Both properties are non-null types; neither can hold `null`.

choices.text: An error, as `minutes` has no default
choices.why: Right: coercion turned `done` into `false` in the third test and left `minutes` failing.

choices.text: The session, because `coerceInputValues` also ignores unknown keys
choices.why: The two settings are independent, and neither key here is unknown.

prompt: Why does the lesson put every setting in one shared `plannerJson` instead of writing `Json { ... }` where it is needed?
hint: Two instances, two sets of rules.

choices.text: Building a `Json` is slow enough to matter on every screen
choices.why: The lesson's argument is consistency, not speed.

choices.text: So that every part of the app reads JSON by the same rules
choices.why: Right: two instances built separately disagree, about unknown keys for example.

choices.text: Retrofit accepts only a top-level `val` as a converter
choices.why: Any `Json` instance can make a converter.

choices.text: `ignoreUnknownKeys` can be set once per process
choices.why: Every instance carries its own settings; that is the problem the shared one avoids.

prompt: Order the payloads of `ServerChangesTest` from the one the default `Json` reads to the one no setting in the lesson rescues.
hint: One works with no setting, one needs `ignoreUnknownKeys`, one is a lost cause.

prompt: Why did the build fail when `SessionDto.date` became a `LocalDate`?
hint: Whose type is `LocalDate`?

choices.text: `LocalDate` needs Android 26, above the module's minimum
choices.why: `minSdk` is 26, and the error was about serializers, not API levels.

choices.text: The plugin has no serializer for Java's `LocalDate`
choices.why: Right: `Serializer was not found for type 'LocalDate'`, at the file and line.

choices.text: A data class cannot hold a `java.time` value
choices.why: `StudySession` holds one already.

choices.text: JSON has no date type, so dates cannot be read
choices.why: A date travels as a string, which the serializer of this section reads.

prompt: The server sends `"date": "27/10/2026"`. What does `LocalDateSerializer` do with it?
hint: `LocalDate.parse` accepts one form.

choices.text: Reads it as 27 October, guessing the order
choices.why: Nothing guesses: `LocalDate.parse` takes ISO 8601 only.

choices.text: Stores the text unchanged in `date`
choices.why: `date` is a `LocalDate`; there is no text to store.

choices.text: Fails at index 0
choices.why: Right: a malformed date is an error, never a wrong date.

choices.text: Uses today's date instead
choices.why: A silent substitute is exactly what the serializer avoids.

prompt: How many class files did `find` list for `SessionDto` once the plugin had compiled it?
hint: The class, its companion and one more.

prompt: Today `toDomain()` copies five fields one to one. When does it earn its place?
hint: Imagine the server renaming a field.

choices.text: Only once the app has two screens
choices.why: The number of screens is not what changes the mapping.

choices.text: When the wire and the model stop matching
choices.why: Right: the DTO and this function change, and nothing else does.

choices.text: Never; it should be deleted until it does something
choices.why: Deleting it puts the DTO back into every screen, which is what section 02 avoids.

choices.text: When Moshi replaces kotlinx.serialization in the app
choices.why: A library swap changes the DTO's annotations, not the mapping's purpose.

prompt: Which default differs between Moshi and kotlinx.serialization in this lesson's tests?
hint: Three of the four payloads gave the same answer.

choices.text: A missing field with no default
choices.why: Both libraries refuse it: `MissingFieldException` and `Required value 'minutes' missing`.

choices.text: A key the class does not declare
choices.why: Right: Moshi ignores `room` by default and kotlinx.serialization refuses it.

choices.text: A `null` for an `Int`
choices.why: Both refuse it, each in its own words.

choices.text: A missing field that has a default
choices.why: Both took `done = false`.

prompt: What does `ksp(libs.moshi.codegen)` add to the build?
hint: Look in `app/build/generated/ksp`.

choices.text: A generator that writes the adapter at build time
choices.why: Right: the adapter is ordinary Kotlin in the build directory.

choices.text: Moshi's runtime library to the app
choices.why: That is `implementation(libs.moshi)`; `ksp(...)` only runs at build time.

choices.text: A reflection fallback for classes without `@JsonClass`
choices.why: Reflection is a separate artifact, `moshi-kotlin`, which this lesson does not use.

choices.text: The compiler plugin that `@Serializable` needs
choices.why: That is the serialization plugin in `plugins { }`, a different tool.

prompt: Match each kotlinx.serialization piece to its Moshi counterpart.
hint: The table at the end of section 06.

prompt: The converter test passed and printed `Method isLoggable in android.util.Log not mocked`. Where did the exception come from?
hint: A unit test compiles against a stub of Android.

choices.text: A bug in the planner's `PlannerApi`
choices.why: The stack trace starts in OkHttp's platform detection, before any planner code ran.

choices.text: A stub `Log` method that throws in unit tests
choices.why: Right: `isReturnDefaultValues = true` makes those stubs return defaults instead.

choices.text: MockWebServer cannot run without an emulator
choices.why: It ran and answered: the test printed both sessions.

choices.text: The `room` key made the converter log a warning
choices.why: `plannerJson` ignores `room` silently; the trace is from OkHttp starting up.

prompt: The test's two sessions add up to how many minutes?
The line that stops stub methods throwing in a unit test is `unitTests.___ = true`.
hint: Section 07's second build file.

prompt: A teammate builds the Retrofit converter from a fresh `Json` instead of `plannerJson`. The server adds a key. What breaks?
hint: Which settings does a fresh `Json` have?

choices.text: Nothing, since Retrofit ignores unknown keys itself
choices.why: Retrofit hands the body to the converter and applies no rules of its own.

choices.text: Only the tests, since phones use a different converter
choices.why: The converter is the same code on a phone and in a test.

choices.text: Every request whose response carries the new key
choices.why: Right: the default `Json` refuses unknown keys, so each such response becomes an exception.

choices.text: The build, at compile time
choices.why: A key in a response is unknown until the response arrives.

prompt: Which of these would make a `StudySession` reach the screen with a wrong value, silently? Choose all that apply.
hint: An exception is loud; a guess is not.

choices.text: A `LocalDate` serializer that returns today's date when parsing fails
choices.why: Yes: the week's total would count the session in the wrong week, and nothing would say so.

choices.text: A DTO with no default for `minutes`
choices.why: No: a missing `minutes` throws, which is loud.

choices.text: A DTO declaring `val minutes: Int = 0`
choices.why: Yes: a session the server sent without a length would show zero minutes.

choices.text: `ignoreUnknownKeys = true`
choices.why: No: it drops keys the app does not use, and every value the app reads is still checked.

prompt: The server renames `course_id` to `courseId`. With the lesson's code, what is the least change, and where?
hint: Which annotation carries the server's name?

choices.text: Remove `@SerialName("course_id")` from `SessionDto`
choices.why: Right: the Kotlin name now matches the wire, and the model and screens do not move.

choices.text: Rename `StudySession.courseId`
choices.why: The model already says `courseId`, and it should not follow the server anyway.

choices.text: Set `ignoreUnknownKeys = false`
choices.why: That would make the app stricter and fix nothing; `course_id` would then be missing.

choices.text: Change `toDomain()` to read the new name
choices.why: `toDomain()` reads the DTO's Kotlin property, which keeps its name.

prompt: Put the steps a response goes through, from the network to the screen.
hint: The converter comes before any Kotlin object exists.
items: OkHttp receives the bytes of the body
